chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Joe Thomas, Emmett Berry and the dispute with Barney Josephson over rehearsals
summary: The band backed acts like Lena Horne and Zero Mostel, and Josephson demanded afternoon rehearsals which Wilson refused.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: But Joe was a great trumpet player, too. Joe did some time with me during the Second World War, and then when Joe left, I forget why -- but I was fortunate enough to get Emmett Berry on trumpet. And he's a swinging trumpet player. And I think that was the band, when I left, I let the band go, and Barney Josephson started getting on me because I didn't rehearse the band. We were a jazz band, but he felt he wasn't getting his money's worth unless we rehearsed, and we were playing for him from eight o'clock at night until four o'clock in the morning, and yet, he wanted us to come in there in the afternoons and rehearse and he'd applaud the music. And he wasn't even featuring the band -- we were there to play for the acts. The band would back up, the drummers would back up Hazel Scott or we'd back up singers like Lena Horne and play bits of music with the comedians like Zero Mostel, and we'd play for the dance, acts, the Crab Sisters, and we'd play the background music for Jimmy Savo and those people, but we weren't featured.
But Josephs didn't feel like he was getting his money's worth -- because we worked eight hours a night, plus we come in there after hours to rehearse. But I just refused to do it, see.
